titles.360: Annotatio II §.I: Three opinions — corporal with bread / transubstitution / spiritual to the faithful
titles.361: Annotatio II §.I: Triple denomination and history — Consubstantiation, Transubstantiation, Spiritual Presence

latin.359: ANNOTATIO II. De Consubstantiatione, Historia ejus Compendiolum complexa ad pag. Aut. 34. & 36. in fin. §. I. IN atque bello Eucharistico, à velitatione verbali rhetorica, de verborum Christi, hoc est corpus meum, interpretatione, propriâ, an impropriâ, ad realem, de ipsius corporis Christi in Sacra Coena praesentia, seu praesentiae potiùs modo, deventum est Disceptationem.
latin.360: Istam cum alii Corporalem pani copulent; Alii annihilatae panis substantiae substituant; Alii denique corporali negatâ, Spiritualem Spiritibus fidelium contingere credant; universi etiam Veritatem sententiae suae ab antiquitate petant & ex ea adstruere fatagant.
latin.361: Triplicis hujus Sententiae cùm triplex Denominatio, tum triplex Historia, Consubstantiationis puta, Transsubstantiationis, & Spiritualis Praesentiae, postliminiò enata est, per compendium à nobis recitanda.
latin.362: Ab istâ tamen ejus parte facto initio, quae nobis in hoc Controversiarum Elencho potissimum opposita est, inque nostra, ceu illius antithesi, postremò defituri, mediam verò, ob solam cum prima cognationem, authore Spanhemio memoratam, duabus nominatis interferturi.

pass_a.359: ANNOTATION II. On Consubstantiation, comprising a little Compendium of its History at the Author’s pp. 34 and 36 at the end. §. I. And in the Eucharistic war, from the verbal rhetorical skirmish about the interpretation of Christ’s words This is my body — proper or improper — it has come to a real Debate about the presence of Christ’s body itself in the Sacred Supper, or rather about the mode of presence.
pass_a.360: When some couple that [presence] Corporally to the bread; Others substitute it for the annihilated substance of the bread; Others finally, the corporal denied, believe a Spiritual [presence] befalls the Spirits of the faithful; all likewise seek the Truth of their opinion from antiquity and labor to build it from that.
pass_a.361: Of this triple Opinion there has afterward arisen both a triple Denomination and a triple History — namely of Consubstantiation, of Transubstantiation, and of Spiritual Presence — to be recited by us in a compendium.
pass_a.362: Yet beginning from that part of it which in this Elenchus of Controversies is chiefly opposed to us, and ending last in ours as its antithesis, but inserting the middle one — mentioned by author Spanhemius for kinship with the first alone — between the two named.

359: Annotatio II opens On Consubstantiation — a short history at Author pp. 34 and 36 fin.
§.I: the Eucharistic war has moved from the verbal fight over whether This is my body is proper or improper to a real debate on Christ’s bodily presence in the Supper — or rather its mode.
360: Three camps: some join a corporal presence to the bread; others put Christ’s body in place of annihilated bread-substance; others deny the corporal and credit a spiritual presence to the spirits of the faithful.
All three hunt antiquity to prove their side.
361: From that triple opinion came a triple name and a triple history: Consubstantiation, Transubstantiation, and Spiritual Presence.
Strimesius will run them in a short compendium.
362: Order: start with Consubstantiation — the part chiefly opposed to us in this Elenchus; end with ours (Spiritual Presence) as its antithesis.
Insert Transubstantiation in the middle only for kinship with the first, as Spanhemius notes.
